references.text: Describes the requirement that sacrificial animals must be without defect to be accepted as an offering to the Lord, reflecting the requirement of 'temimim' (without defect) in Numbers 28:19.
Refers to a burnt offering to the Lord during the Feast of Unleavened Bread, which is the same context as Numbers 28:19.
Mentions similar offerings with lambs, bulls, and rams as burnt offerings to the Lord.
Basic instructions regarding the daily burnt offering with unblemished lambs, forming the basis for festival offerings.
Parallel sacrificial regulation for the New Moon day with the same types of animals: two bulls, one ram, and seven lambs.
Similar sacrificial regulation for the Day of Trumpets with a burnt offering of bull, ram, and lamb.
Burnt offering on the Day of Atonement with the same type of sacrificial animal as in Numbers 28:19.
Ezekiel's vision of future temple offerings during Passover week, with seven bulls and seven rams daily for seven days.
Christ's sacrifice as the ultimate fulfillment of unblemished burnt offerings, cleansing our conscience.
